mechanisms.definition: A versioned JSON root binds meshes, materials, nodes, camera, light, world, quality tiers and Android targets.
mechanisms.integration: Creates one inspectable authority record for Python, glTF and native packing.

mechanisms.definition: Each node stores finite translation, normalized quaternion rotation and nonzero 3-axis scale.
mechanisms.integration: Provides stable transform semantics across reference and native runtimes.

mechanisms.definition: Rotations reject zero quaternions and normalize valid values before matrix or simulation use.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents drift and invalid rotation matrices.

mechanisms.definition: Meshes use stable IDs, finite 3D vertices, triangle indices and optional per-vertex normals.
mechanisms.integration: Shared source for glTF and KC3D391.

mechanisms.definition: Missing vertex normals are accumulated from incident face cross products and normalized.
mechanisms.integration: Keeps primitive/custom meshes renderable without external libraries.

mechanisms.definition: Materials carry base color, metallic, roughness, emissive and double-sided state.
mechanisms.integration: Maps into retained PBRMaterial and native shader uniforms.

mechanisms.definition: Nodes select none, sphere or box collider records with validated dimensions and sensor state.
mechanisms.integration: Provides low-cost mobile collision proxies.

mechanisms.definition: Validation requires each node mesh/material reference and node ID to be resolvable and unique.
mechanisms.formula: node.mesh in MeshIDs and node.material in MaterialIDs
mechanisms.integration: Prevents deployment-time dangling references.

mechanisms.definition: Camera position/target/up, FOV and near/far planes are validated for nondegenerate projection.
mechanisms.integration: Shared by CPU preview, glTF intent and GLES renderer.

mechanisms.definition: A finite nonzero light direction, nonnegative color/intensity and bounded ambient term define mobile shading.
mechanisms.integration: Feeds the dependency-free Lambert/rim native shader.

mechanisms.definition: Each tier declares target FPS, render scale, visible-node budget, MSAA, post and shadow level.
mechanisms.integration: Allows deterministic capability selection and runtime degradation.

mechanisms.definition: A profile declares SDK levels, ABIs, GLES, refresh, memory floor, hints and default quality.
mechanisms.integration: Separates device policy from scene/game content.

mechanisms.mechanism: POCO X7 Pro 12 GB signature profile
mechanisms.definition: An ARM64 profile recognizes POCO X7 Pro/Mali-G720 hints and selects the 120 Hz ultra tier when capability floors pass.
mechanisms.integration: Primary optimized target requested for this edition.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented + host-tested; device profiling not claimed

mechanisms.definition: Fallback profiles cover high-end, mainstream and compatibility Android classes.
mechanisms.integration: Keeps the same project deployable beyond one phone model.

mechanisms.definition: Runtime selection scores model/GPU hints, RAM, GLES and refresh support with deterministic tie-breaking.
mechanisms.integration: Picks a safe starting profile without hard failure on unknown phones.

mechanisms.definition: Build/runtime callers may request a named target instead of automatic scoring.
mechanisms.integration: Supports reproducible benchmarks and device-specific variants.

mechanisms.definition: The reference world advances by an explicit fixed time step and sorted entity order.
mechanisms.integration: Provides deterministic gameplay fixtures independent of rendering.

mechanisms.definition: Dynamic velocity and position integrate a declared gravity vector per fixed step.
mechanisms.integration: Basic arcade motion shared with the native demo.

mechanisms.definition: Collider vertical extent constrains dynamic nodes to the floor and applies bounded restitution.
mechanisms.integration: Provides stable grounding and bounce suppression.

mechanisms.definition: X/Z position is clamped to declared bounds and velocity reflects with restitution.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents mobile demo actors escaping the arena.

mechanisms.definition: Sphere and box colliders expose a bounding radius for deterministic pair testing.
mechanisms.integration: Keeps collision cost predictable for reference/gameplay use.

mechanisms.definition: Penetrating dynamic pairs receive mass-weighted correction and normal impulse restitution.
mechanisms.integration: Adds conventional arcade collision response without claiming a full rigid-body engine.

mechanisms.definition: Normalized 2-axis input maps to X/Z velocity at a declared player speed.
mechanisms.integration: Shared semantics for headless tests and native controls.

mechanisms.definition: Jump velocity is applied only when the player is in grounded contact.
mechanisms.integration: Avoids unlimited airborne jumps in the reference loop.

mechanisms.definition: Sensor overlap with a player despawns a collectible and increments score.
mechanisms.integration: Provides a complete mobile gameplay loop.

mechanisms.definition: Player overlap with a goal marks the world finished and emits a goal event.
mechanisms.integration: Defines a deterministic completion condition.

mechanisms.definition: Player overlap with a hazard decrements bounded health and emits damage.
mechanisms.integration: Demonstrates tagged interaction semantics.

mechanisms.definition: World settings, sorted entities, state and events serialize to canonical JSON and SHA-256.
mechanisms.integration: Supports replay fixtures and deterministic regression checks.

mechanisms.definition: A cube factory emits face-separated vertices and normals for crisp mobile shading.
mechanisms.integration: Provides a dependency-free production primitive.

mechanisms.definition: A plane factory emits a Y-up quad with validated width/depth.
mechanisms.integration: Supplies arena ground geometry.

mechanisms.definition: A pyramid factory emits base/side triangles and synthesized normals.
mechanisms.integration: Adds low-cost stylized geometry.

mechanisms.definition: A latitude/longitude sphere factory emits positions, normals and valid indexed triangles.
mechanisms.integration: Supports player, collectibles and collider visualization.

mechanisms.definition: Mobile projects convert to the existing 3.0 Scene/Asset/Node model without changing source authority.
mechanisms.integration: Reuses established scene hashing, preview and export paths.

mechanisms.definition: The retained glTF writer materializes mobile meshes, nodes, transforms and PBR material mappings.
mechanisms.integration: Provides external 3D inspection/interchange.

mechanisms.definition: Native packs start with an eight-byte magic, endian marker, format version and bounded record counts.
mechanisms.integration: Enables early rejection of wrong or unsupported files.

mechanisms.definition: The pack declares little-endian encoding before numeric records.
mechanisms.integration: Makes byte-order assumptions testable.

mechanisms.definition: Strings use uint16 byte lengths and reject oversized/truncated records.
mechanisms.integration: Avoids external serialization libraries and unbounded reads.

mechanisms.definition: Vertices store float32 position/normal pairs followed by uint32 indices.
mechanisms.integration: Uploads directly into GLES vertex/index buffers.

mechanisms.definition: Materials serialize base color, metallic, roughness, emissive and double-sided state.
mechanisms.integration: Maps directly into native render uniforms.

mechanisms.definition: Nodes serialize references, transforms, velocities, collider, mass, restitution and tag mask.
mechanisms.integration: Carries scene and lightweight gameplay data into Android.

mechanisms.definition: A Python reader verifies all sections, references, hashes and exact end-of-file consumption.
mechanisms.integration: Provides release evidence without Android tooling.

mechanisms.definition: The app uses Android native_app_glue callbacks for window, focus, input and destruction.
mechanisms.integration: Keeps managed-code dependencies out of the runtime core.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: Scene loading, profile selection, fixed-step gameplay, rendering and input live in native C++.
mechanisms.integration: Delivers the requested native source target.

mechanisms.definition: The renderer selects an ES3 window configuration, creates EGL context/surface and enables swap pacing.
mechanisms.integration: Broad Android renderer baseline with no third-party engine.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: GLSL ES 3 vertex/fragment shaders load from APK assets and compile/link with diagnostics.
mechanisms.integration: Keeps shader source editable in the Android project.

mechanisms.definition: The renderer enables depth testing and material-aware back-face culling.
mechanisms.integration: Supports practical opaque 3D scenes.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: The scene renders to an offscreen color/depth target sized by quality render scale and blits to the surface.
mechanisms.integration: Reduces fragment cost while preserving full-screen presentation.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: The runtime dynamically resolves ANativeWindow_setFrameRate and requests the selected target FPS.
mechanisms.integration: Allows 120 Hz intent on supported displays while retaining older-device fallback.

mechanisms.definition: Left-side touch displacement maps to bounded X/Z movement input.
mechanisms.integration: Provides controller-free phone play.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: Right drag adjusts yaw/pitch and two-pointer spacing adjusts camera distance.
mechanisms.integration: Supports direct mobile 3D inspection/play.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: WASD/D-pad, Space/A and joystick axes share the same movement/look state.
mechanisms.integration: Supports Android controllers and desktop/emulator testing.
mechanisms.validation: Implemented; Android build not executed here

mechanisms.definition: Model, manufacturer, GPU renderer, RAM, CPU cores, GLES and refresh hints feed profile selection.
mechanisms.integration: Moves device tuning from compile-time assumptions into runtime policy.

mechanisms.definition: Quality descends after sustained stress and recovers only after a longer comfortable interval.
mechanisms.integration: Avoids immediate oscillation and prioritizes thermal stability.

mechanisms.definition: The POCO flavor limits output to arm64-v8a and forces the signature profile.
mechanisms.integration: Produces a focused device-target source configuration.

mechanisms.definition: The universal flavor includes arm64, ARMv7 and x86_64 with automatic profiles.
mechanisms.integration: Supports phones, older devices and emulators from one project.

mechanisms.definition: The source pins compile/target SDK 36, min SDK 26, AGP 8.13.2, Gradle 8.13 and NDK r29.
mechanisms.integration: Makes reproducible Android setup requirements explicit.

mechanisms.definition: The C++ pack parser, POCO profile selector and quality controller compile and execute on the release host.
mechanisms.integration: Validates cross-language deployment logic without Android SDK claims.

mechanisms.definition: Generated Android projects include a file/hash report, project hash, backend and toolchain metadata.
mechanisms.integration: Supports auditing and regeneration.

mechanisms.definition: Manifest/project metadata reserve optional Vulkan capability while 3.9.1 stays GLES3.
mechanisms.integration: Prevents an optional hook from becoming a false implementation claim.

mechanisms.definition: A draft distinguishes spacetime gameplay from four-spatial-dimensional geometry and requires metric/projection contracts.
mechanisms.integration: Makes the requested 4D possibility actionable without overstating delivery.
